verses.1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowd and his disciples.
verses.2: They said: “On Moses’ throne, the scribes and the Pharisees sat.”
verses.3: So, whatever you have done and kept to your promises, do not do the same for them. They certainly don’t do what they promise either.
verses.4: They impose heavy burdens on people’s backs, and they also cause great suffering to them. They themselves do not want to move those burdens with their arms.
verses.5: But they always carry out their tasks so that people can see them. After all, their prisons become larger, and their towers grow taller.
verses.6: They also love to hold banquets and celebrate important events during gatherings.
verses.7: And those who participate in the competitions, and are called by people’s names… Rabbi.
verses.8: You should not be called “teacher”. Rabbi, after all, is your teacher. You are all brothers.
verses.9: And do not call your father on earth; for your father is indeed the heavenly Father.
verses.10: And do not even call yourselves teachers, for your teacher is Christ himself.
verses.11: The greater of you will be your deputy.
verses.12: For whoever raises himself up will be humiliated, and whoever humbles himself will be elevated.
verses.13: But you, officials and Pharisees, who pretend to be righteous, you shut out the kingdom of heaven from those who are beneath you. For you do not allow those who are above you to enter, nor do you allow those who have been invited to enter.
verses.15: O you scribes and Pharisees, you deceive those who are near the sea and those who live in the desert, making them believe that you can turn the sea into dry land. And when you do this, you make them your children.
verses.16: Oh, you blind guides! Who among us would be happy to stay in a ship? There’s nothing to be gained from that. And who among us would be happy to stay in the gold of the ship itself?
verses.17: Are those who are impure and blind more important than gold or those who have sanctified the gold?
verses.18: And as for those who are present in the altar during the sacrifice, they don’t owe anything. But those who are present above the offering, they do owe something.
verses.19: The blind ones, what is more important: the gift or the altar, or the act of worship?
verses.20: So, he also cries in the altar, and in all those who are above him.
verses.21: And the same thing happens in the ship as well; it affects both the ship itself and the person who lives on it.
verses.22: And the omniscient one also sings in heaven, in God’s throne, and in the place where He sits above all others.
verses.23: You, officials and Pharisees, who are deceivers! You have abandoned the righteous, the holy, and the kind-hearted people. You have also abandoned the most important things of the law: judgment, mercy, and faithfulness. These things should still be carried out by you.
verses.24: Those guides were blind; they could neither see nor understand anything.
verses.25: Do you, you scribes and Pharisees, pretend to be clean when it comes to washing the outside of your mouths and noses? But inside, we are covered in filth from stealing and robbery.
verses.26: The pharisee is blind; first, clean the mouth of the bottle and its spout, so that the contents inside can also be made clean.
verses.27: Do you, you scribes and Pharisees, deceive yourselves? You compare these tombs to beautiful houses. On the outside, they seem beautiful, but inside, they are filled with dead bodies and all kinds of filth.
verses.28: In this way, although you may seem fair to people from the outside, inside, you are actually full of injustice and corruption.
verses.29: O you scribes and Pharisees, you deceive yourselves by claiming that you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the memorials to the righteous.
verses.30: And you say, “If we were alive in the days of our fathers, would we not have been united with them in the blood of the prophets?”
verses.31: So that you may testify to yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
verses.32: And you have fulfilled the measure of your fathers.
verses.33: Oh, creations of the gods! How could you escape from the judgment of God?
verses.34: Therefore, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. From them, you will get guidance. Use them to spread the word of God among your people. Drive them out from one city to another.
verses.35: So that all justice may be done upon you, with every drop of blood spilled on the ground, from the blood of Abael the Just, down to the blood of Zacharias, son of Barachius, whom you slaughtered between the temple and the altar.
verses.36: Indeed, I say to you, all these things will happen in this lifetime.
verses.37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You who destroyed the prophets and sent those who were sent to you away—how many times have I wanted to bring your children here, like birds that are carried away by the wind. But you didn’t want to do that.
verses.38: See, your home is now empty and desolate.
verses.39: I say to you, do not wait until dawn before you speak. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.
